Sheet 3

HIGH COURT A.M.
Mr Kam appeared for the S M C

Proceedings.

Accused:- I know Tsang Choong, he was a school teacher
with me but he was dismissed for bad teaching. I am not able to say
if he is a communist or not, but I am not a communist.

Dong Paa Representative of the S.J. :-I have outlined
my evidence and have produced the dispatch warrant for the handing
over of the accused. He was arrested on the 15.10.34. on instructions
from the Shanghai Koosemg Land quarters of the Garrison.

Accused:- I know Tsung Chi Tso as he was a friend of
Tsang Choong. I never went with them or assisted them in forming the
"Tso Los Party" and I did not give $10.00 to that party.

Mr Kam:- Here is photo of a communistic nature that
was found ( photo produced ).

Accused:- The photo is the property of Tsang Choong.

Mr Kam:- The S M C/S M Police have no objection for the
handing over of the accused.

Decision.
T/B
Accused to be handed over together with the seized property
to the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau.
HANGCHOW 17.10.34.

MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 6122
Date 19 / 10 / 34

October 19 34.

Dear Mr. Sarly,

I forward herewith tabulated statement relating
to the arrest of a communist named Cheu Tao Sung alias
Cheu Tao Sin alias Cheu Yoong at noon October 15,1934,
at No.32/117 Pingliang Road. The accused appeared
before the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on
October 17,1934 and was ordered to be extradited to the
Chinese Authorities.

Copy of photograph of Cheu Tao Sung is attached.

Yours sincerely,

（签名）

Monsieur. R. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police.

Subject (in full) Case against Cheu Tao Sung (邱道声) alias Cheu Tao Sin (邱陶心)
alias Cheu Yoong (邱永) charged with being a communist.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [签名]

Regarding the case against Cheu Tao Sung (邱道声) alias
Cheu Tao Sin (邱陶心) alias Cheu Yoong (邱永) who was arrested
by the Municipal Police on the authority of a warrant issued at
the instance of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau at 32/117
Pingliang Tshung (平凉邨), Pingliang Road, at 12 noon 13.10.34,
on a charge of being a communist, which was concluded on
October 17, 1934, when the accused was ordered to be extradited
to the Chinese Authorities, I forward herewith a tabulated
statement referring to this individual together with a
draft of a covering letter to the French Police relating
to this case.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch

(邱陶Sin) alias Cheu Yoong (邱永).

being a communist.

Extradited to Chinese Authorities on 17.10.34.

Acting on the authority of a warrant issued at the
instance of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau, the Municipal
Police visited the Woo Tung Commercial & Business School,
32/117 Pingliang Tshung, Pingliang Road, and arrested the
accused. A single sheet pictorial depicting an armed struggle
between policemen and labourers found among his personal effects
was seized. The accused appeared on remand before the Second Branch
Kiangsu High Court on October 17 when he was ordered to be
extradited to the Chinese Authorities.

Charge Application is hereby made to the S.S.D.Court for by the
Shanghai Public Bureau for the handing over of the above described
person who was arrested at 12 noon on the 13/10/34 at the Woo
Tong Commercial and Business School, 82/117 Pingliang Road under
the authority of S.S.D.Court Warrant No 4349 on a charge of being
a communist.

Proceedings:-

Mr. Kum appeared for the Council.
(Warrant No. 4347 and 361 handed to Judge)

Mr. Kum:- Accused is suspected of being a communist and he was
arrested at 11.50 a.m. on 13.10.34. on assistance rendered to Tong
Pau, representative of Public Safety Bureau who was armed with a
warrant issued by the S.S.D.Court for the arrest of accused and Zung
Chong. Police accompanied the representative to Lane 117 house 32
Pinliang Road where the accused was arrested and the Zung Chong was
not located. A map (produced) was found in his box and it was given
to him by a communist. Accused said his name is not Cheu Tao Sing
but a chop for the same has been found (produced) Accused said the
map was given to him by Zung Chong in school but he denied of being
a communist. The representative of Public Safety Bureau can
prove that he is a communist.

Representative Tong Pau:- On instruction from Nanking Government
that a man arrested in Nanking implicating the accused of being a
communist and giving his address in Shanghai. After applied the
warrant from S.S.D.Court I went to Wayside Police Station asking for
assistance to proceed to Lane 117 house 32 Pingliang Rd. to make
the arrest. On arrival only the accused was arrested. I ask
for a remand to enable Public Safety Bureau to produce the despatch
for handing over of the accused. Accused admitted to Police that
the seized chop is his.

Accused:- My name is Cheu Tao Sung. This map was given to me
by Zung Chong who was dismissed 2 weeks ago for bad teaching. I am

Acting on the authority of a warrant issued at
the instance of the local Bureau of Public Safety, the
Municipal Police at 12.50 p.m. October 13, 1934,
visited the Woo Tong (滬東) Commercial and Business
School, 32/117 Pingliang Tshung (平涼邨), Pingliang
Road, and effected the arrest of one Cheu Tao Sung
(邱濤声) alias Cheu Tao Sin (邱陶心) alias Cheu Yoong

armed struggle between policemen and labourers found
among the effects of the accused was seized. The
accused appeared before court on October 15 when the
case against him was remanded until October 17 .

My name is Chou Tao Sung ( 邱 濤 松 ) age 25,
native of Shaocrow, single, a school teacher employed and
residing at the Woo Tung ( 吳 東 ) Commercial & Business
School, 32/117 Pingliang Tsiming, Pingliang Road off
Yangtsepoo Road.
        I came to Shanghai in July, 1933 to seek
employment, and took up residence in Boppe Terrace, Rue
Dubail, French Concession.    Four months later, I obtained
a post as editor in the Chung Hsueh Sung ( 中 學 生 ) Bookstore,
60 Hoong Yuen Fong ( 鴻 運 坊 ) off Ward Road, and resided
on the premises.    In May 1934 I was tranferred to a branch
store at No. 7 Yung Chih Li ( 永 吉 里 ) off Rue Chapsal,
French Concession, again residing on the premises.    A
month later I obtained my present post as teacher at the
Woo Tung Commercial & Business School, and have resided in
the school ever since.
        I came to Shanghai direct from Canton by the ss. Kung
Ping of the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company.    On
arriving here I had $100 in my possession given to me by
my father in Canton.    I had not previously done any work,
having studied in the Feng Yung ( 馮 庸 ) University, Peiping,
for the two years ending
for xxxxxxxxx May 1, 1933, following a
preparatory course of study at the Central University ( 中 央 )
of Nanking and the Shih Mei ( 集 美 ) Middle School, Amoy.
        I obtained my first post in Shanghai through the
recommendation of a student named Vung Soo Meng ( 文 苏 夢 )
